description:
# SNP Demux [![CI](https://github.com/swarbricklab/snp_demux/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/swarbricklab/snp_demux/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Snakemake](https://img.shields.io/badge/snakemake-%E2%89%A57.32.4-brightgreen.svg)](https://snakemake.github.io) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) [![Code style: snakefmt](https://img.shields.io/badge/code%20style-snakefmt-000000.svg)](https://github.com/snakemake/snakefmt) This workflow demultiplexes "pooled captures". A "pooled capture" is when multiple tissues samples are dissociated into single cells together in the same test tube, and then captured together using the 10X Chromium platform to generate scRNA-seq libraries. ```mermaid flowchart LR SA["Sample A"] --> POOL SB["Sample B"] --> POOL SC["Sample C"] --> POOL POOL["Dissociate and pool
into one tube"] --> CAP["10x Chromium
capture"] CAP --> LIB["scRNA-seq library
barcode of origin unknown"] GT["Donor SNP profiles
(VCF)"] --> DEMUX LIB --> DEMUX{{"SNP demultiplexing"}} DEMUX --> OA["Sample A"] DEMUX --> OB["Sample B"] DEMUX --> OC["Sample C"] DEMUX --> OD["Heterotypic
doublets"] ``` When these libraries are sequenced, it is not obvious which cell barcode came from which sample. But by utilizing SNP profiles for each sample in the pool, we can attempt to demultiplex the capture by assigning each barcode to an individual sample. We can also use SNP information to detect "heterotypic doublets", where a barcode represents a doublet of two cells, each from a different sample. ## Contributions This workflow is a simplification and refactoring of the [demuxafy](https://github.com/swarbricklab/demuxafy) workflow developed by [Daniel Roden](https://github.com/dlroden) and [Beata Kiedik](https://github.com/BeataKiedik). The demuxafy workflow is, in turn, a Snakemake wrapper around the [Demuxafy](https://demultiplexing-doublet-detecting-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html) package and tools developed by [Drew Neavin](https://github.com/drneavin) at the Powell Lab. The main difference between this workflow and the [demuxafy](https://github.com/swarbricklab/demuxafy) workflow is that several phases have been factored out into separate, reusable workflows that are prerequisites for this one: - [genotyping](https://github.com/swarbricklab/genotyping) and [imputation](https://github.com/swarbricklab/imputation) — build the donor SNP-genotype panel; - [sc_pileup](https://github.com/swarbricklab/sc_pileup) — the expensive, deterministic **per-cell pileup** (cellSNP-lite, popscle `dsc-pileup`, souporcell `vartrix`). snp_demux no longer computes pileups: it **consumes sc_pileup's outputs** and runs only the (comparatively fast) demultiplexing + consensus. This means the pileups can be frozen and the demux re-run and re-tuned cheaply, and it greatly simplifies this workflow's rule graph (see below). ## Method Briefly, this workflow runs four well-established SNP demux methods in parallel and then uses [Demuxafy](https://demultiplexing-doublet-detecting-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html) to call doublets and find a consensus sample-barcode assignment. The four methods are 1. vireo [docs](https://vireosnp.readthedocs.io/en/latest/)| [paper](https://genomebiology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13059-019-1865-2) | [GitHub](https://github.com/single-cell-genetics/vireo) 2. souporcell [paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-020-0820-1) | [GitHub](https://github.com/wheaton5/souporcell) 3. demuxlet [docs](https://github.com/statgen/demuxlet/blob/master/tutorial/README.MD) | [paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/nbt.4042) | [GitHub](https://github.com/statgen/demuxlet) 4. freemuxlet [GitHub](https://github.com/statgen/popscle) See the links above for details on the algorithms used by each of these methods. The results of each method are combined using Demuxafy's [AtLeastHalfSinglet](https://demultiplexing-doublet-detecting-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/CombineResults.html) option, but there is scope to extend this workflow to include other options for combining results. ### souporcell cluster annotation souporcell is genotype-free: it clusters barcodes by SNP profile but cannot name the clusters. The workflow maps those clusters onto the known donor genotypes twice, by two independent routes: 1. Demuxafy's own correlation-based matching, which feeds the consensus above. 2. [vireoSNP](https://vireosnp.readthedocs.io/en/latest/), which scores each cluster against each donor genotype and is run separately. The vireoSNP annotation is appended to the combined results as an additional assignment column *after* the consensus has been called, so it does not influence it. The barcode-level output therefore carries five assignments per cell — `Demuxlet`, `Freemuxlet`, `Souporcell`, `Vireo` and `Souporcell_vireosnp` — plus the `AtLeastHalfSinglet` consensus over the first four. Treating vireoSNP as a fifth opinion is useful when reviewing a capture: it is the only assignment derived from a genotype-free clustering that was named after the fact. ### Ambient RNA vireo estimates the fraction of ambient RNA per barcode as a by-product of assignment. The workflow summarises this per capture into a distribution over bins, which is a useful first check when a capture has an unexpectedly high doublet rate or a low singlet fraction. At a high level of abstraction, the overall processing flow is as follows: ```mermaid flowchart TB IN["Barcodes, BAM and donor genotypes"] IN --> DL["demuxlet
genotype-aware"] IN --> VI["vireo
genotype-aware"] IN --> FM["freemuxlet
genotype-free"] IN --> SO["souporcell
genotype-free"] DL --> DX VI --> DX FM --> DX SO --> DX DX["Demuxafy
matches the genotype-free clusters to donors
by correlation, then calls the
AtLeastHalfSinglet consensus"] SO --> VS["vireoSNP
names souporcell's clusters
independently"] DX --> OUT["One assignment per barcode from each
method, plus the consensus"] VS -. "appended after
the consensus" .-> OUT ``` ### Rule graph Because the pileups are produced upstream by [sc_pileup](https://github.com/swarbricklab/sc_pileup) and consumed here, the rule graph contains **only** the demultiplexing, consensus, aggregation and reporting rules — no per-cell pileup, per-chromosome split, or merge rules: ![snp_demux rule graph](docs/rulegraph.svg) Each engine reads sc_pileup's output for the capture (`cellSNP.*` for vireo, `pileup.{cel,var,plp,umi}.gz` for demuxlet/freemuxlet, `ref/alt.mtx` for souporcell) and the per-pool donor-genotype panel; nothing re-reads the BAM. ## Requirements This workflow requires, per capture: 1. **sc_pileup outputs** — the per-cell pileups produced by [sc_pileup](https://github.com/swarbricklab/sc_pileup) (cellSNP-lite, popscle `dsc-pileup`, souporcell `vartrix`), under `deps.pileup_root`. 2. **A per-pool donor-genotype panel** — the donors' SNP profiles at the piled sites, as `deps.panel_root//informative.vcf.gz` (bgzipped + `.csi`-indexed). The cellranger `barcodes.tsv.gz` and `possorted_genome_bam.bam` are inputs to **sc_pileup** (which reads the BAM once to build the pileups); snp_demux itself never re-reads the BAM. Run [sc_pileup](https://github.com/swarbricklab/sc_pileup) first against the panel's sites, then point `deps.pileup_root` at its output root. Before running, make sure the panel and BAM satisfy the tool requirements (all-autosome coverage, matching contig order, a populated `R2` field for demuxlet) — see [`docs/data_prep_requirements.md`](docs/data_prep_requirements.md). ### `cellranger` barcodes (for sc_pileup) sc_pileup takes the following `cellranger` "outs": 1. `barcodes.tsv.gz` 2. `possorted_genome_bam.bam` In particular, the `barcodes.tsv.gz` file under `filtered_bc_matrix` should be preferred over the `raw_bc_matrix`, because `cellranger` filters out empty droplets and other low-quality barcodes. Excluding these barcodes should improve the performance and accuracy of this workflow. > Theoretically, it may be possible to further improve performance and accuracy by further filtering the barcode list, based on criteria such as gene counts, mitochondrial content or other doublet detection methods. > However this theoretical benefit has not been benchmarked. ### VCF file This workflow has been tested with SNP profiles based on microarray data. Raw microarray data (`.CEL` files) for each donor sample can be aggregated into an appropriate VCF file via the [genotyping](https://github.com/swarbricklab/genotyping) workflow. The resulting VCF can be used directly as an input to this workflow. Alternatively, additional SNPs can be imputed based on the 1000 Genomes project via the [imputation](https://github.com/swarbricklab/imputation) workflow. Imputation provides more SNPs and therefore a better chance of finding matching reads in sparse scRNA-seq data, which [apparently](https://demultiplexing-doublet-detecting-docs.readthedocs.io/_/downloads/en/v0.0.3/pdf/) yields better results but we have not benchmarked this. > (*) Note that SNP profiles do not have to be generated from the same tissue as the sample being demultiplexed. > We get good results with other tissues from the same donor, including blood samples. Our experience so far is with SNP profiles based on SNP microarrays, but theoretically VCF files derived from whole genome sequencing should also work, if appropriately filtered to exclude non-SNP variants. > Note: make sure that the chromosome notation (`chr1`, `chr2`, .. versus `1`, `2`, ...) in the VCF file matches that used by the reference transcriptome specified with `cellranger`. ## Configuration The workflow is driven by a single config file, passed with `--configfile`. See [`config/template_config.yaml`](config/template_config.yaml) for a starting point. | Key | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `deps.samples` | Sample sheet: which samples are in which capture (see below) | | `deps.captures` | Capture sheet: one row per capture (see below) | | `deps.pileup_root` | Root of the sc_pileup outputs consumed here: `////` | | `deps.panel_root` | Per-pool donor-genotype panels: `//informative.vcf.gz`. Defaults to `/panel` | | `deps.default_platform` | Platform used when a capture row has no `platform` column (default `short`) | | `deps.vcf` | Legacy cohort donor VCF; retained for reference. Donor genotypes now come per-capture from the panel above | | `outs.root` | Root for all data outputs | | `outs.logs` | Root for per-rule logs | | `outs.reports` | Optional. Where the HTML reports are written; defaults to `/report` | | `params.cellsnp_lite` | Legacy pileup thresholds; the pileup is now done upstream in sc_pileup, so these are unused here | | `params.demuxlet` | `coeff` and `offset` for the demuxlet doublet prior | | `params.demuxafy` | Correlation limits for matching souporcell and freemuxlet clusters to donors, and the agreement threshold for the consensus | | `ref.souporcell.genome_fasta` | Reference genome FASTA, matching the transcriptome used by `cellranger` | | `containers.*` | Per-tool container images (replaces the old monolithic Demuxafy.sif): `bcftools`, `popscle` (demuxlet/freemuxlet), `vireo` (demux CLI), `vireosnp` (souporcell-genotyping + cell counts), `souporcell`, `r` (all R/Rmd rules), `demuxafy` (consensus/summary/assign scripts). See `config/template_config.yaml` and the recipes under [`containers/`](containers) | Set `outs.reports` when the reports should be published alongside a dataset's other reports rather than buried in the data tree. For example, in a dataset repository: ```yaml outs: root: data/snp/demux/ logs: logs/snp/demux reports: reports/snp_demux ``` ### Sample sheets `captures.csv` — one row per capture: ```csv capture_id,pool_id,barcodes,bam,cells_captured,possible_live_cells Mixed_1,Mixed_1,path/to/barcodes.tsv.gz,path/to/possorted_genome_bam.bam,15000,12000 ``` `pool_id` is optional and is used only to group captures in the reports. Leave it blank if the captures are not organised into named pools. `cells_captured` and `possible_live_cells` are carried for provenance and are not read by the workflow. `samples.csv` — one row per sample per capture: ```csv sample_id,donor_id,capture_id DONOR_1,DONOR_1,Mixed_1 DONOR_2,DONOR_2,Mixed_1 ``` `sample_id` identifies the sample in the pool; `donor_id` identifies the genotype in the VCF. These differ when several samples come from one donor, for example a primary and a metastasis. The number of rows for a capture sets the number of clusters souporcell, freemuxlet and vireo are told to look for, so this sheet must be complete. The donor-genotype panel and the BAM must satisfy a few tool requirements (all-autosome coverage, matching contig order, a populated `R2` field for demuxlet) — see [`docs/data_prep_requirements.md`](docs/data_prep_requirements.md). ## Running ### Preflight the inputs Before a full run, validate each capture's donor panel against the [input requirements](docs/data_prep_requirements.md): ```bash snakemake check_inputs --workflow-profile profiles/workflow ``` This read-only check (one `check_panel` per capture) confirms the `informative.vcf.gz` panel spans every autosome (chr1–chr22), carries an `R2` INFO value on every site, and is contig-ordered to match Cell Ranger — the three things that otherwise surface as cryptic popscle/demuxlet FATALs partway through a run. It is not part of `rule all`, so running or skipping it cannot change any demux result. ### The pipeline This module is defined as a [Snakemake](https://snakemake.readthedocs.io/en/v7.32.3/) workflow. The pipeline is roughly as follows. This is a simplification: each box stands for a group of rules. The per-cell pileups are produced upstream by [sc_pileup](https://github.com/swarbricklab/sc_pileup) and consumed here, so this workflow starts from those pileups and the donor panel — it does not read the BAM or run the pileup/split/merge steps itself (see the full rule graph above). ```mermaid flowchart TB PANEL["donor panel
informative.vcf.gz"] PLP["sc_pileup outputs
(cellSNP · popscle · souporcell pileups)"] PLP --> DL["demuxlet"] PANEL --> DL PLP --> FM["freemuxlet"] PANEL --> FM PLP --> VI["vireo"] PANEL --> VI VI --> AMB["ambient RNA
summary"] PLP --> SO["souporcell"] PANEL --> SO SO --> VS["vireoSNP
cluster annotation"] DL --> DX FM --> DX VI --> DX SO --> DX DX["Demuxafy consensus"] --> ASSIGN VS --> ASSIGN ASSIGN["sample_barcode_assignments.tsv
per capture"] --> STATS["cell counts
per sample"] ASSIGN --> COMB["combined_results.tsv
all captures"] STATS --> REP["HTML reports"] AMB --> REP COMB --> REP ``` Run it from the root of the dataset repository: ```bash bash modules/snp_demux/run_mod.sh ``` On NCI, `run_mod.sh` loads `singularity`, activates the `snakemake_7.32.4` environment and selects the cluster profiles under [`profiles/`](profiles), which submit each job to PBS. Elsewhere it runs locally. Any additional arguments are passed through to `snakemake`, so `--dry-run`, `--until` and friends work as usual. The DAG is large — well over a hundred jobs per capture — so build it on a compute node rather than a login node. After `snakemake` finishes, `run_mod.sh` does two clean-up steps: 1. Deletes the empty placeholder PNGs that `relabel_vireo` creates to trigger downstream rules when a capture has no unknown genotypes. 2. Appends the per-rule logs to `.tar.gz` and removes the directory. This workflow produces tens of thousands of small log files, which is a real problem on a shared filesystem with an inode quota. The archive is appended to, not recreated, so an incremental run keeps the logs of every capture run previously. ## Outputs ``` / demuxlet// per-method results freemuxlet// souporcell// souporcell/annotation/vireosnp// vireo// ambient_stats.csv ambient RNA fraction, binned ambient_summary.csv ambient_plot.png assignment// sample_barcode_assignments.tsv one row per barcode, all five methods plus consensus cell_assignment.tsv all_cells_stats.tsv cells per sample, including doublet and unassigned all_singlets_stats.tsv cells per sample, singlets only assignment/report/ combined_results.tsv all captures, stamped with capture_id all_cells_stats_full.tsv all_singlets_stats_full.tsv ``` `sample_barcode_assignments.tsv` is the main result. > Note on reading these files: sample ids are frequently bare digits, so a TSV > reader left to infer types will read `sample_id` as numeric for some captures > and character for others, and the two then refuse to join. Always declare the > expected column types. ## Reports The workflow renders a set of linked HTML pages under `outs.reports`: ``` / index.html captures/.html metrics/.tsv ``` `index.html` is the landing page: - **Overview** — singlet fraction across all captures, and a callout naming any declared sample that was not recovered as a singlet. - **By capture** — one row per capture. - **By sample** — one row per sample per capture, so searching a sample id finds every capture it appears in, plus a listing of samples spanning more than one capture. Both tables are filterable per column and export to CSV, and every capture id links through to its page. Each capture page covers: - **Summary** — barcodes, singlets, doublets, unassigned, samples declared vs recovered, ambient RNA. - **Cell counts by sample** — as a share of all barcodes and as a share of singlets. - **Ambient RNA** — the binned distribution, plus vireo's genotype-distance figure. - **Agreement between methods** — the calls each method made, how many methods back the consensus for each barcode, and the pairwise concordance between methods. - **Method diagnostics** — the freemuxlet correlation and vireoSNP matching heatmaps. Figures are embedded rather than linked, so a capture page can be sent on its own. The `metrics/.tsv` files are the per-capture roll-up that both the capture page and the index read, so the two cannot disagree. ## Reproducibility Every rule runs in a pinned container (the Demuxafy-toolchain images are pinned to the exact versions the retired `Demuxafy.sif` shipped), and all demultiplexing **calls** reproduce byte-for-byte given the same frozen pileups + panel. The one output that is *not* bit-reproducible is vireo's ambient-RNA proportion QC (`--callAmbientRNAs` uses multithreaded, non-associative float reductions) — it does not affect any donor assignment. See [`docs/reproducibility.md`](docs/reproducibility.md) for the container pins, the full list of what is / isn't reproducible, and how the container split was verified against the `Demuxafy.sif` baseline. ## Validation Reproducibility (above) proves **determinism**; separately the pipeline is validated for **correctness**. On the *full* OneK1K pool, `sc_pileup → snp_demux` reproduces the per-method demultiplexing numbers Neavin et al. publish for Demuxafy: freemuxlet and souporcell match at default settings, and vireo matches once cellSNP thresholds are matched to theirs. The comparison tables, methodology, and the one-off full-depth run configs (`config/test_config.full{,_neavin}.yaml`) are in [`docs/validation/demuxafy_consistency.md`](docs/validation/demuxafy_consistency.md).
name: snp_demux: a Snakemake workflow for SNP-based single-cell demultiplexing
